clue.text: Great flow of letters leaving a warm feeling

indicators.note: the letters of the two words leave their places and settle in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A great outpouring of correspondence leaves its readers feeling warm inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letters leaving' tells you to reshuffle the letters of GREAT FLOW; 'of' simply joins the fodder to that signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The glow left after a pleasant experience is a lingering warm sensation, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Supplier paid with a sovereign

parts.note: paid can be read as fee'd, given a fee
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the sovereign

explanation.surface: A supplier receives payment in the form of a gold coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sovereign' looks like the gold coin but gives ER, the royal cipher of the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that supplies or feeds another, like a tributary or a feeder road, is a supplier.

clue.text: Waugh's name elevated in uniform fashion

indicators.note: in a down clue elevated means one letter is lifted higher up the word

parts.note: the novelist Evelyn Waugh's first name

explanation.surface: The novelist's name is raised, delivered in an even manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elevated' moves the N of EVELYN up two places in this down light, giving E-V-E-N-L-Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something evenly means doing it regularly and consistently, in a uniform way.

clue.text: Flighty Scots female student wearing a waistcoat

indicators.note: the waistcoat is worn around the student, so it holds the letter inside

parts.note: a gilet is a sleeveless jacket or waistcoat
L is a learner, the plate on a learner driver's car

explanation.surface: A giddy Scottish girl at college dons a sleeveless waistcoat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' puts L inside GILET. The answer is a Scots word for a giddy, flighty young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots dialect this word names a giddy or skittish young girl, matching flighty female.

clue.text: South Africa paper's leading material

indicators.note: the paper is placed in front, leading the South African letters

parts.note: a newspaper can be called the organ of a party or body
ZA is the international code for South Africa

explanation.surface: A South African newspaper sells its leading story about a fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leading' is an indicator on the charade, putting the paper first; ZA comes from Zuid-Afrika, the country's vehicle and internet code.
explanation.definitionFit: Organza is a thin stiff silk or synthetic fabric, so it is a dress material.

clue.text: If this were you wouldn't get it

definitions.text: If this were you wouldn't get it

parts.words: If this were you wouldn't get it
parts.note: a clue that could not be cracked would leave you unable to work it out: the word for a problem with no solution

explanation.walkthrough: The clue talks about itself: a puzzle without a solution would be one you never get.
explanation.definitionFit: A problem that cannot be solved is described with this word, which also means not dissolving.

clue.text: A model inspector at cricket, say …

definitions.text: A model inspector at cricket, say

parts.words: A model inspector at cricket, say
parts.note: someone who watches a cricket match does nothing but look on, a perfect example of an observer

explanation.walkthrough: 'inspector' tempts you to think of police; here it means one who looks, as a member of the crowd at a cricket match does.
explanation.definitionFit: An onlooker at a sporting event is a watcher, the ideal example of one who inspects.

clue.text: … to watch first in — a startling sight

parts.note: to eye something is to watch it
in cricket the opening batsman, the opener, is first in to bat

explanation.surface: Continuing from the previous clue, watching the first batter come out proves a surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links back to the cricket of 7: the opener is the batsman who goes in first.
explanation.definitionFit: Something revealing or surprising that opens one's eyes is a startling sight.

clue.text: Watch taking forty winks — that's smart!

indicators.note: the watcher takes the short sleep inside itself

parts.note: to spy is to watch
forty winks is a nap, a short sleep

explanation.surface: Someone on guard dozes off, and an observer calls that clever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Watch' looks like a noun for a timepiece but is a verb, and 'forty winks' is a well-known idiom for a short doze.
explanation.definitionFit: Snappy can describe stylish, smart dress, as in a snappy dresser.

clue.text: Top brass lost right to go back with unknown pedigree

indicators.note: the officer loses one letter, which is taken out

parts.note: a general is one of the top brass, the senior officers

indicators.note: go back means the little word is read in reverse

parts.note: Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A senior officer loses his rights and is sent back with no known lineage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' removes the right from the officer, leaving GENEAL; 'back' reverses the little word so it reads OG; the unknown follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A family's pedigree is its line of descent, which is what this study of ancestry traces.

clue.text: Fashion item partly based upon choice

indicators.note: only part of the words upon choice is used, the run sitting across them

explanation.surface: Choosing an outfit is partly based on personal preference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partly' points to the letters running across 'upon choice'; 'based' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A poncho is a cloak with a hole for the head, a garment worn as a fashion item.

clue.text: Oil supplier met an explosion that was not malicious

parts.note: an oil well supplies oil

indicators.note: an explosion blows the letters apart into a new order

explanation.surface: An oil well suffers an explosion, but it was accidental, not sabotage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'explosion' rearranges the letters of 'met an' after the oil supplier; the surface makes the explosion sound literal.
explanation.definitionFit: An action done with good intentions, even if it goes wrong, is free of malice.

clue.text: Minister consumed by dog

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
consumed means ate

explanation.surface: A clergyman is eaten by a dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' here just means next to, not a container signal, and 'Minister' is a clergyman rather than a politician.
explanation.definitionFit: A curate is an assistant to a parish priest, a minister of the church.

clue.text: This type finds it hard to swallow anything not solid

definitions.text: This type finds it hard to swallow anything not solid

parts.words: This type finds it hard to swallow anything not solid
parts.note: a doubter cannot swallow, that is believe, any claim not soundly based; the surface suggests someone who cannot eat solids

explanation.walkthrough: 'swallow' means believe and 'solid' means well founded, not a diet of liquids.
explanation.definitionFit: A doubting person who cannot accept flimsy claims is described as distrustful in this way.

clue.text: Summoning for reprimand for taking trouble over Fido?

indicators.note: the taking trouble part goes over the pet, holding it inside

parts.note: caring means taking trouble over someone
Fido is a stock name for a dog, an example of a pet, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: Someone goes to great lengths to look after their dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' places the dog inside the caring. To carpet someone is British slang for calling them in for a telling-off.
explanation.definitionFit: Being called on the carpet means being summoned to the boss for a reprimand.

clue.text: Space traveller — about which I do more to unravel

indicators.note: the unravelled letters go about the little alien, enclosing it
unravel means the letters of I do more are untangled into a new order

parts.note: which refers back to the space traveller, the film alien ET

explanation.surface: An alien visitor considers what more to do to solve a mystery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to unravel' turns I DO MORE into M-EOROID, and 'about' wraps that round ET, the space traveller 'which' points back to.
explanation.definitionFit: A meteoroid is a small rocky body travelling through space.

clue.text: Mother turns cross

indicators.note: turns means the word is read the other way round

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal

explanation.surface: Mum turns angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' reverses DAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Being mad in the informal sense means being angry, which is what cross means.

clue.text: Calumny in Bermuda?

indicators.note: the letters are found inside the word Bermuda

explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points inside BERMUDA for the three letters. Mud as in mud-slinging means slander.
explanation.definitionFit: Slinging mud is spreading slanderous accusations, so it means calumny.

clue.text: Name and return address in America

indicators.note: return means the letters come back in reverse

parts.note: bud is an American form of address to a man, like pal

explanation.surface: Give your name and return address in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return address' reads as postal; 'return' reverses BUD, an American way of addressing someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To dub someone is to give them a name or title.

clue.text: Little potato with water at a country seat

parts.note: a chat is a small potato
eau is French for water

explanation.surface: Small potatoes and water served at a country house.
explanation.walkthrough: CHAT is a dialect word for a small or inferior potato; EAU is the French for water.
explanation.definitionFit: A French castle or manor house is a grand residence in the country.

clue.text: Free one soul in agony

indicators.note: a soul in agony is writhing, so its letters twist into a new order

explanation.surface: Release a single soul suffering torment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in agony' rearranges ONE SOUL.
explanation.definitionFit: To unloose is to set loose or release, a synonym of free as a verb.

clue.text: One came out and went back there to sleep

indicators.note: went back means the place for sleep is read in reverse

parts.note: a bed is where one goes to sleep

explanation.surface: A girl went out, then went back home to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'came out' means made a debut in society; a deb is a debutante.
explanation.definitionFit: A debutante is a young woman making her formal entrance, or coming out, into society.

clue.text: First letter is open, perhaps letter from abroad

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the letters could be arranged differently
first means just the opening letter of the word letter

explanation.surface: The first letter is open, perhaps a letter sent from overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First letter' gives L, which 'perhaps' shuffles with IS OPEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsilon is the fifth letter of the Greek alphabet, a foreign letter.

clue.text: Man's little friend, such a one with strings attached

parts.note: a dog is man's best friend, and a little dog is a pup
a pup is such a one as a pet

explanation.surface: A man's small companion is his pet, a creature on a lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strings attached' suggests conditions; here it is a marionette worked by strings.
explanation.definitionFit: A marionette is moved by strings, so it is literally a figure with strings attached.

clue.text: Herb is far from 6

definitions.meaning: an old name for a medicinal herb
6 down describes a problem that cannot be solved; the opposite is easy

explanation.walkthrough: 6 refers to 6-down; something easy is far from impossible to solve.
explanation.definitionFit: Simple means easy, the very opposite of a problem with no answer.

clue.text: Last in managed to settle

indicators.note: managed suggests the letters have been handled and rearranged

explanation.surface: The last one in managed to settle down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'managed' rearranges LAST IN. This is a variant spelling of install.
explanation.definitionFit: To install oneself somewhere is to settle into place.

clue.text: Support for those subject to invasion by soldiers

definitions.text: Support for those subject to invasion by soldiers

parts.words: Support for those subject to invasion by soldiers
parts.note: soldiers are strips of toast dipped into soft-boiled eggs, which sit in a small holder

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, 'soldiers' are fingers of toast dunked into a boiled egg, not troops.
explanation.definitionFit: A small cup holds a boiled egg upright while it is eaten, supporting it.

clue.text: Phone-tapping, for example, is page one material

indicators.note: the words are raw material to be refashioned into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Bugging telephones makes front-page news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'material' rearranges IS PAGE ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Tapping phones is an instance of spying, which this word names.

clue.text: Lock up alien taken from the web

indicators.note: the alien is removed, taken out of the larger word

parts.note: the web is the internet
ET is the film alien, the extra-terrestrial

explanation.surface: Imprison a foreigner caught online.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken from' removes ET from INTERNET.
explanation.definitionFit: To intern someone is to confine them, especially in wartime, which is locking them up.

clue.text: Farcical performance that hits credit

parts.note: slaps means hits
tick is British slang for credit, as in buying on tick

explanation.surface: A comic show that is a smash on credit.
explanation.walkthrough: To buy 'on tick' is British for buying on credit.
explanation.definitionFit: Slapstick is boisterous physical comedy, a kind of farce.

clue.text: A 20 for the Beeb

parts.note: 20 across means free, so to untie

explanation.surface: A cross-reference for the BBC.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Beeb' and this answer are both British nicknames for the BBC.
explanation.definitionFit: The BBC is affectionately called by this family nickname, as it is by the name Beeb.

clue.text: Cut in gnarled tree without having to be intrusive

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: without means outside, so the gnarled letters surround the cut
gnarled means twisted, so the letters of tree are twisted into a new order

parts.note: to lop is to cut

explanation.surface: Pruning a gnarled tree without permission is an intrusion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gnarled' turns TREE into TERE, and 'without' (meaning outside) wraps that round the cut; 'in' simply leads.
explanation.definitionFit: To interlope is to intrude into others' affairs, so it means to be intrusive.
